question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core-owned skill permission manifest contract, and should the first phase be audit-only metadata, install-time consent, or enforced capability gating?
rationale: This choice defines a public security boundary across skills, ClawHub, plugin hooks, install/update UX, signing roots, and runtime enforcement, so automation should not pick the permanent contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt staged audit-only manifest
options.body: Define a small versioned skill permission vocabulary first, expose it in status/install-policy surfaces, and track consent, enforcement, signing, and attestation as explicit follow-ups.

options.title: Design full enforcement first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers settle default-deny runtime enforcement, approval UX, update diffs, and migration behavior together.

options.title: Keep manifest outside core
options.body: Treat external packages and ClawHub scan pages as the primary permission surface unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Adopt staged audit-only manifest
recommendation.body: Define a small versioned skill permission vocabulary first, expose it in status/install-policy surfaces, and track consent, enforcement, signing, and attestation as explicit follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the most direct product/security decision signal in the issue discussion and already framed the remaining work as maintainer follow-up.
